extracted.intended_audience: State education agencies (SEAs), local education agencies (LEAs), school leaders, and potential grant applicants (schools, IHEs, nonprofits, tribes)
extracted.subtask_description: A reference guide enumerating allowable uses of funds, program-level requirements, and eligible entities under ESSA (Every Student Succeeds Act) for state and local education agencies and other grant applicants. It lists program activities (e.g., prevention/intervention, parent engagement, professional development, early childhood), standards for those activities, and which entities may receive funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention and intervention for neglected, delinquent, or at-risk youth (Title I, Part D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs to support children and youth who are neglected, delinquent, or at-risk, including worksite schools (IHEs/employers partnerships), programs supporting reentry of youth offenders (age 20 or younger) into postsecondary education or career and technical training, programs serving children returning from correctional facilities to assist transition and school retention, and dropout prevention programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategies may include essential support services such as personal, career and technical, and academic counseling; placement services to place youth in university/college/junior college programs; information and assistance obtaining student financial aid; counseling services; and job placement services. Also includes programs providing mentoring and peer mediation and programs for at‑risk Indian children in correctional facilities. Eligible entities: SEAs, one or more LEAs, other public agencies, or private nonprofit organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination of health and social services for at-risk youth
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordination of health and social services when such services (including day care, drug and alcohol counseling, and mental health services) are likely to improve the likelihood that individuals will complete their education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended as a coordinated wraparound to increase school completion among targeted youth served under prevention/intervention programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services to children in local institutions (neglected/delinquent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing services to children in local institutions for neglected children, and to children in local institutions for delinquent children and neglected or delinquent children in community day programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These activities fall under Title I, Part D allowable uses and are targeted at institutionalized children and those in community programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent and family engagement activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses of funds to support parent and family engagement including disseminating best practices, collaborating with community organizations, providing literacy training (if other funds exhausted), and supporting programs that reach parents at home, in the community, and at school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: disseminating information on best practices focused on increasing engagement of economically disadvantaged parents; collaborating/providing subgrants to enable schools to collaborate with organizations with a record of success; providing necessary literacy training if other resources are exhausted; supporting schools/nonprofits to provide PD for LEA and school personnel on family engagement strategies; paying reasonable and necessary expenses (including transportation and child care) to enable parent participation; implementing effective engagement strategies, programs, activities, and procedures. Eligible entities: LEAs, community-based organizations, Indian tribes or tribal organizations, other public or private entities, or consortia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parenting skills and family literacy programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding may be used for parenting skills programs that promote parental involvement and family literacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are allowable under parent/family engagement uses and may be delivered by LEAs or community partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing or expanding teacher/principal/school leader preparation academies
rubrics_metrics.description: States may establish or expand teacher, principal, or other school leader preparation academies, enable candidates attending such academies to be eligible for State financial aid on the same terms as other State-approved programs, and allow teachers/principals working while on alternative certificates to teach while enrolled in an academy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities may include establishing or expanding academies if allowable under State law; enabling financial aid parity with other preparation programs; and enabling working candidates to participate. Eligible entity: SEAs (and Grants to LEAs where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reforming/improving preparation programs via residencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reforming or improving teacher, principal, or other school leader preparation programs, such as through establishing teacher residency and school leader residency programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reforms are intended to strengthen preparation through hands-on residency models and practical training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reforming certification, licensing, and tenure systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Reforming teacher or principal certification, recertification, licensing, or tenure systems and preparation program standards and approval processes to ensure teachers and school leaders have necessary subject-matter knowledge and instructional leadership skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may require measures determined by the State (which may include teacher performance assessments) to demonstrate subject-matter knowledge. Reforms should align certification/licensing requirements with State academic standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing best practices among early childhood providers and transition supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing best practices among early childhood program providers to increase collaboration and efficiency of services and improve transitions from early childhood programs to elementary school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities include convening providers, disseminating effective strategies, and improving coordination for child transitions into K‑12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic statewide needs assessment for early childhood programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducting a periodic statewide needs assessment of availability and quality of existing early childhood programs, including service to vulnerable/underserved populations and rural areas, and, to the extent practicable, unduplicated counts of children served and children awaiting service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should identify gaps, vulnerable populations, and capacity constraints to inform strategic planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximizing parental choice and information in early childhood mixed delivery systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximizing parental choice and knowledge about the State’s mixed delivery system by ensuring parents receive information about the variety of early childhood programs and promoting involvement by parents, including low-income families, in child development and transitions to elementary school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes outreach and information provision so parents can make informed choices among providers in the mixed delivery system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing and implementing a strategic plan for early childhood coordination and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: After a needs assessment, develop a strategic plan recommending collaboration, coordination, and quality improvement activities (including transition activities), identifying partnership opportunities (Head Start, LEAs, State/local government, tribes, private entities), building on existing plans and Federal/State statutory requirements, and describing how activities will better serve children and increase participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic plans should describe activities, barriers and opportunities for collaboration, and how the plan will increase service and participation; they should incorporate relevant statutes (e.g., Child Care and Development Block Grant Act) and reports when appropriate. Eligible entity: Governor-appointed State entity (Preschool Development Grants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve quality of early childhood programs using evidence-based practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Improving overall quality of early childhood education programs by developing and implementing evidence-based practices that meet ESSA requirements to improve professional development for providers and educational opportunities for children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should, where practicable, implement evidence-based interventions and professional development to raise program quality and align with ESSA evidence requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality, personalized, evidence-based professional development
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing high-quality, personalized professional development that is evidence-based (to the extent evidence is reasonably available, as determined by the State in consultation with LEAs) for teachers, instructional leadership teams, principals, or other school leaders focused on improving teaching and student learning and achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include assistance to LEAs to develop/implement PD for principals, PD that addresses literacy, numeracy, remedial or other LEA needs, and PD that may lead to advanced credentials. Services may be made freely available to LEAs via partnerships or publicly accessible electronic means. Eligible entities vary by program (SEAs, LEAs, IHEs, nonprofits).

rubrics_metrics.name: American history, civics, and geography professional development
rubrics_metrics.description: Expanding, developing, implementing, evaluating, and disseminating innovative, evidence-based PD approaches or programs in American history, civics and government, and geography that show potential to improve student achievement and teaching in these subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs must demonstrate innovation, scalability, accountability, and focus on underserved populations; may include hands-on civic engagement activities and education about the Constitution and Bill of Rights. Eligible providers include IHEs, national nonprofits with demonstrated effectiveness, partnerships, and BIE. Also includes establishing a Presidential Academy: a seminar/institute led by primary scholars and core teachers, conducted in summer or appropriate time, duration not less than 2 weeks and not more than 6 weeks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on formative and classroom‑based assessments and data use
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing training, technical assistance, and capacity-building to assist teachers, principals, or other school leaders with selecting and implementing formative assessments, designing classroom-based assessments, and using assessment data to improve instruction and student achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities may include providing additional time for teachers to review student data and respond as appropriate. PD should include training on protecting student privacy as required under FERPA and state/local laws when using data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrating career and technical education into academic instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting PD and improving instructional strategies to integrate career and technical education content into academic instructional practices, including training on best practices to understand State and regional workforce needs and transitions to postsecondary education and the workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to align K‑12 instruction with workforce and postsecondary transition needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training to prevent and recognize child sexual abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing training for all school personnel — including teachers, principals, other school leaders, specialized instructional support personnel, and paraprofessionals — regarding how to prevent and recognize child sexual abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to PD activities across LEAs and relevant entities to build capacity for prevention and identification of abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional development to support dual/concurrent enrollment and early college
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing PD activities that enhance or enable the provision of postsecondary coursework through dual or concurrent enrollment programs and early college high school settings across an LEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets teachers, principals, and other school leaders to expand access to postsecondary opportunities in high schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early childhood professional development and early childhood literacy initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Carrying out high-quality PD opportunities for early childhood educators, teachers, principals, paraprofessionals, specialized instructional support personnel, and instructional leaders; and training providers and personnel to develop and administer evidence-based early childhood literacy initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes programs to increase knowledge on early grades instruction and strategies to measure young children's progress; joint professional learning and planning activities addressing preschool-to-elementary transitions; and training to teach children with disabilities and English learners (may include multi-tier systems of support and positive behavioral interventions and supports). Eligible entities include LEAs, for-profit/nonprofit entities through LEA grant/contract, partnerships with IHEs, tribes, institutions of higher education, national nonprofits with demonstrated effectiveness, and other organizations with demonstrated expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: PD for teaching children with disabilities and English learners
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing programs and activities that increase teachers' ability to effectively teach children with disabilities (including significant cognitive disabilities) and English learners, which may include use of multi-tier systems of support and positive behavioral intervention and supports, so such children can meet State academic standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to ensure inclusive instruction and use of evidence-based multi-tiered supports and behavioral strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiential learning and observation opportunities in PD
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing PD that supports participation in opportunities for experiential learning through observation for teachers, principals, or other school leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include structured observation experiences as part of personalized PD to improve instructional practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible entities and provider requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification of entities eligible to receive funds or provide services, varying by program: LEAs; for-profit or nonprofit entities through a grant/contract from an LEA; LEA partnerships with IHEs, Indian tribes, or tribal organizations; SEAs; institutions of higher education; national nonprofits with demonstrated record of effectiveness; partnerships consisting of such entities and for-profits; Bureau of Indian Education; nonprofit educational organizations, museums, libraries, research centers, or consortia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is program-specific and often requires demonstrated record of effectiveness or partnership structures; check program statutory citations (e.g., Title II, Title I, Preschool Development Grants) for exact eligibility rules.
